### Fig. 1(a)
- quantity: metric = AUROC; dataset set = ALL5; fraction or level = 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0; kind = clean test performance; statistic = dataset-averaged mean (the 95% CI band is drawn but has no numbers-book key)

- CI: {"method": "nested percentile bootstrap of the dataset-averaged mean", "B": 5000, "seed": 42, "interval": "95% percentile [2.5, 97.5]", "resampling": "the 10 splits are resampled with replacement within each dataset, then averaged over datasets"}
- splits: `n-outer-splits` = 10; datasets: `n-datasets` = 5

- numbers-book keys displayed: 28 (see figure_facts.json)
- sources:

- caveats (verbatim):
  - **CKD**: The paper's statements about CKD must say it is saturated, and results must be reported both with and without it
  - **UNIT**: the Friedman tests and critical-difference diagrams are **descriptive only**, because the BLOCK unit is anti-conservative (the 10 splits of a dataset come from overlapping-training-set repeated cross-validation) and the DATASET unit has essentially no power (minimum possible two-sided Wilcoxon p = 0.0625 with 5 datasets, 0.125 with 4)

### Fig. 1(c)
- quantity: metric = calibration slope (Platt, pooled); dataset set = per NO_CKD dataset (dots + bootstrap whiskers) and NO_CKD mean (bar); fraction or level = 0.1; kind = clean test predictions; statistic = pooled slope
- items shown: logreg, rf, xgb, lgbm, mlp, ftt, tabnet; 4 datasets: pima_diabetes, heart_cleveland, ilpd, breast_wisconsin
- symbols: colour = model; marker SHAPE = dataset (o pima_diabetes, s heart_cleveland, ^ ilpd, D breast_wisconsin); whiskers = bootstrap CI of the pooled slope; black horizontal bar = NO_CKD mean of the 4 pooled slopes; dotted horizontal line at slope 1 (perfect calibration slope); log y axis
- CI: {"method": "percentile bootstrap of the pooled slope (per dataset)", "B": 2000, "seed": 42, "interval": "95% percentile [2.5, 97.5]", "resampling": "the 10 splits are resampled with replacement; replicates with separable classes are dropped (column n_dropped_replicates); NO CI exists for the NO_CKD-average bar, none is drawn"}
- splits: `n-outer-splits` = 10; datasets: `n-datasets-no-ckd` = 4
- exclusions: ckd is excluded from the slope panel and its NO_CKD average: saturated dataset with extreme pooled slopes (CLAUDE.md sections 6-7)
- numbers-book keys displayed: 91 (see figure_facts.json)
- sources:
  - `results/phase3b/calibration_metrics.csv` sha256 `2a0206c0b59336924c7f7fd94021f0c344959d19c2c4a2eb3302cb7b53150ef9` -- fraction == 0.1, dataset in NO_CKD (pima_diabetes, heart_cleveland, ilpd, breast_wisconsin); column slope = one dot per dataset (panel c)
  - `results/phase3b/calibration_bootstrap_ci.csv` sha256 `1b2f1e8dc6b75c7d60a431beb5be8fcf5bc4ccc86c161c90fddd4121a426e7de` -- fraction == 0.1, same datasets; whiskers = slope_lo/slope_hi (per-dataset bootstrap CI)
  - `results/phase3b/calibration_averaged.csv` sha256 `6d199d7bc7da0240ecbd51f7f713dace0fb9fffe93c27f17e24a8db252b6975c` -- fraction == 0.1, dataset_set == NO_CKD; column slope_mean = black bar. No CI exists for the NO_CKD average, so none is drawn.
- caveats (verbatim):
  - **CAL1**: every pooled calibration analysis uses 2 x n_rows predictions per (dataset, model, fraction), since each test row appears in 2 of the 10 splits (one per CV repeat). ECE on small samples is biased and noisy
  - **CAL2**: use Brier and log loss as primary calibration measures, with bootstrap confidence intervals.
  - **CKD**: The paper's statements about CKD must say it is saturated, and results must be reported both with and without it

## Fig. 2 -- `fig_main_robustness`
- files: fig_main_robustness.png (300 dpi), fig_main_robustness.pdf
- size: 7.16 x 2.2 in (2148 x 660 px)

### Fig. 2(a)
- quantity: metric = AUROC; dataset set = ALL5; fraction or level = 30% missing; noise 0.5; kind = missing (MCAR) and original Gaussian noise; statistic = change versus the model's own clean AUROC (degradation), dataset-averaged
- items shown: logreg, rf, xgb, lgbm, mlp, ftt, tabnet
- symbols: two groups on the x axis (30% missing, noise 0.5); one marker per model with vertical CI whisker (colour and marker per model); filled markers
- CI: {"method": "percentile bootstrap of the dataset-averaged mean change", "B": 5000, "seed": 42, "interval": "95% percentile [2.5, 97.5]", "resampling": "the 10 splits are resampled with replacement within each dataset (between-dataset variability is ignored)"}
- splits: `n-outer-splits` = 10; datasets: `n-datasets` = 5
- exclusions: none (ALL5)
- numbers-book keys displayed: 14 (see figure_facts.json)
- sources:
  - `results/phase3c/robustness_averaged.csv` sha256 `31f96f892770ad5feb7d79cd9160655e4217d211aa763dd003cfa8192f741196` -- dataset_set == ALL5; panel a: kind==missing level==0.3 and kind==noise level==0.5, metric==auroc, degradation_mean with degradation_ci_lo/hi; panel b: kind==noise level==0.5, metric==log_loss (filled markers)
- caveats (verbatim):
  - **ROB1**: every result describes MODEL + the saved pipeline's IMPUTER together (median/most-frequent imputation fitted on the training fold is part of the pipeline), not the model in isolation; tree models use no native NaN handling. Missingness tested is MCAR only
  - **ROB2**: Degradation is always relative to each model's OWN clean performance on that split, so a model with lower clean performance can show smaller absolute degradation.
  - **NOISE**: Noise is relative to each column's TRAINING standard deviation and applied to ordinal numeric columns (CKD `sg`/`al`/`su`, Cleveland `ca`) as if continuous.

### Fig. 2(b)
- quantity: metric = log loss; dataset set = ALL5; fraction or level = noise 0.5; kind = original and continuous-only Gaussian noise; statistic = change versus the model's own clean log loss (degradation), dataset-averaged
- items shown: logreg, rf, xgb, lgbm, mlp, ftt, tabnet
- symbols: FILLED markers = original noise; OPEN (white-filled) markers = continuous-only noise variant; one marker per model with CI whisker
- CI: {"method": "percentile bootstrap of the dataset-averaged mean change", "B": 5000, "seed": 42, "interval": "95% percentile [2.5, 97.5]", "resampling": "the 10 splits are resampled with replacement within each dataset (between-dataset variability is ignored)", "note": "original noise: B above; continuous-only variant: B = 5000"}
- splits: `n-outer-splits` = 10; datasets: `n-datasets` = 5
- exclusions: continuous-only variant excludes ordinal columns (CKD sg/al/su, Cleveland ca) from the noise
- numbers-book keys displayed: 14 (see figure_facts.json)
- sources:
  - `results/phase3c/robustness_averaged.csv` sha256 `31f96f892770ad5feb7d79cd9160655e4217d211aa763dd003cfa8192f741196` -- dataset_set == ALL5; panel a: kind==missing level==0.3 and kind==noise level==0.5, metric==auroc, degradation_mean with degradation_ci_lo/hi; panel b: kind==noise level==0.5, metric==log_loss (filled markers)
  - `results/phase3d/noise_continuous/noise_cont_averaged.csv` sha256 `335402187d0e5bc5404c5631a1886e6b7889bf9efec19986120ead12c0889b94` -- dataset_set == ALL5, kind==noise_cont level==0.5, metric==log_loss (open markers, panel b)
- caveats (verbatim):
  - **ROB1**: every result describes MODEL + the saved pipeline's IMPUTER together (median/most-frequent imputation fitted on the training fold is part of the pipeline), not the model in isolation; tree models use no native NaN handling. Missingness tested is MCAR only
  - **ROB2**: Degradation is always relative to each model's OWN clean performance on that split, so a model with lower clean performance can show smaller absolute degradation.
  - **NOISE**: Noise is relative to each column's TRAINING standard deviation and applied to ordinal numeric columns (CKD `sg`/`al`/`su`, Cleveland `ca`) as if continuous.

## Fig. 3 -- `fig_main_explanations`
- files: fig_main_explanations.png (300 dpi), fig_main_explanations.pdf
- size: 7.16 x 2.4 in (2148 x 720 px)

### Fig. 3(a)
- quantity: metric = top-5 Jaccard of SHAP importances; dataset set = per dataset (all 5); fraction or level = fraction 1.0 pipelines; kind = pairs logreg-rf, logreg-mlp, rf-mlp; within-model stability (mean over models); chance level; statistic = mean over the 10 splits
- items shown: pairs logreg-rf, logreg-mlp, rf-mlp; within-model stability; chance level; 5 datasets on the x axis
- symbols: pair markers: o logreg-rf, ^ logreg-mlp, D rf-mlp (neutral greys); open black square = within-model stability (mean over models); black cross = chance level; no CI drawn
- CI: {"method": "none drawn in panel (a)", "note": "the CI columns jaccard_ci_lo/hi of agreement_per_dataset.csv are not plotted"}
- splits: `n-outer-splits` = 10; datasets: `n-datasets` = 5
- exclusions: none
- numbers-book keys displayed: 25 (see figure_facts.json)
- sources:
  - `results/phase3d/agreement_per_dataset.csv` sha256 `ac38fe19e46a617e890c4615519308fd94d023c663baaa3ae3ba6635b0328a6a` -- all 5 datasets; model pairs logreg-rf, logreg-mlp, rf-mlp; column jaccard_mean = dots (panel a)
  - `results/phase3d/baselines.csv` sha256 `204b0fdc09ac6010e013f0cf1859f250cd404a97b89ce381c652054be7a938a1` -- type == within_model_mean_over_models (squares, jaccard_mean) and type == chance (crosses, jaccard_mean) (panel a)
- caveats (verbatim):
  - **EXPL**: so only RANKINGS (top-5 sets, Spearman correlation) are ever compared across models, never raw SHAP magnitudes.
  - **CORR**: Correlated features — especially Breast Wisconsin's mean/standard-error/worst triplets — can substitute for one another in a top-5 set
  - **C9**: Pairs with cross-model Jaccard BELOW within-model stability: 13 of 15.

### Fig. 3(b)
- quantity: metric = plausibility precision of the top-5 against the pre-registered list; dataset set = per dataset (all 5); fraction or level = fraction 1.0 pipelines; kind = logreg, rf, mlp; statistic = mean precision with 95% CI, and chance precision
- items shown: logreg, rf, mlp; 5 datasets on the x axis
- symbols: colour and marker per model with CI whisker; black cross = chance precision; DAGGER (†) on a dataset tick label = chance precision >= 0.60 (plausibility non-informative, claim map C10)
- CI: {"method": "percentile bootstrap of the mean precision over the 10 splits", "B": 5000, "seed": 42, "interval": "95% percentile [2.5, 97.5]", "resampling": "the 10 splits are resampled with replacement"}
- splits: `n-outer-splits` = 10; datasets: `n-datasets` = 5
- exclusions: none
- numbers-book keys displayed: 60 (see figure_facts.json)
- sources:
  - `results/phase3d/plausibility.csv` sha256 `f047be2981c6c475e996ba763f716be87c024f5ac3d604e381f4c4901a306a45` -- models logreg, rf, mlp; precision_mean with precision_ci_lo/hi (dots, 95% CI) and chance_precision (crosses) (panel b). DAGGER (†) on a dataset tick label of panel b = chance precision >= 0.60, i.e. plausibility non-informative (claim map C10); define it in the caption
- caveats (verbatim):
  - **DIR**: No direction-of-effect (positive/negative SHAP) check was performed.
  - **C10**: Datasets flagged non-informative (chance >= 0.60):
